css-reorder-tab-vs-visual-meaning: CSS like flexbox order or absolute positioning rearranges the page so it reads one way visually but Tab moves focus in the unrelated DOM order, confusing keyboard users.
interleaved-focus-between-semantic-group: Tabbing through a form jumps back and forth between two unrelated sections instead of finishing one before starting the next, breaking the user's sense of what belongs together.
f85-revealed-dialog-not-adjacent: Clicking a button opens an in-page dialog or menu, but pressing Tab next lands on unrelated page content instead of inside the thing that just appeared.
f85-focus-return-after-dismissal: After closing a dialog, focus is dumped at the top of the page instead of returning to the button that opened it, stranding keyboard users.
modal-focus-not-contained-both-direction: A popup dialog looks like it blocks the page, but pressing Shift+Tab or Tab at its edge lets focus slip out to the hidden content behind it.
multiple-valid-orders-row-vs-column: A grid or table of controls can legitimately be tabbed either row-by-row or column-by-column, so flagging the column-wise order as broken would be a false alarm.
nested-and-static-focusable-illogical-st: Making a wrapper div or plain text focusable adds pointless or duplicate Tab stops, so keyboard users land on the same control twice or pause on dead content.
f44-positive-tabindex-breaks-meaning: Hand-numbered tabindex values force Tab to visit controls in an order that contradicts the content's logical sequence, scrambling the experience for keyboard users.
